neighbours.label: ' of' right after a government office title, leading into its portfolio (Minister of Health, minister of justice, Secretary of State, Ministry of Finance); ' of' after other heads (cup of, Duke of, University of, Bishop of) stays quiet
fire: Yesterday the Minister of Education opened the new campus.
Under the constitution, the minister of defence commands the reserve forces.
A letter from the Minister of Agriculture reached every farm in the district.
During the summit, the Secretary of State met her counterpart twice.
Last year the Ministry of Transport cancelled the tunnel project.
In his memoir the former Minister of Finance describes the crisis.
The delegation was welcomed by the Minister of Tourism at the airport.
Reporters asked the deputy minister of labour about the strike.
quiet: Yesterday the University of Lisbon opened the new campus.
Under the old custom, the Duke of Norfolk leads the procession.
A letter from the Bishop of Lincoln reached every parish in the district.
During the summit, the Prime Minister met her counterpart twice.
Last year a group of engineers cancelled the tunnel project.
In his memoir the former captain of the team describes the final.
The delegation was welcomed with a cup of tea at the airport.
Reporters asked the mayor about the cost of the strike.

notes: Card: ' of' x20 and ' Minister' x6 of the top 32, in minister/secretary titles. Probes: Minister of Health 0.59, minister of justice 0.60, Ministry of Finance 0.43, Commissioner of Police 0.47, Secretary of State 0.36; weaker for Department of 0.29, Director of 0.28, Chancellor of 0.20, Governor of 0.16; Bishop of 0.02, Duke of 0.04, University of 0.04, cup of 0.01. 'Minister for' also fired (0.33), so the title matters more than the word 'of'.
